Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Uma Chetry and Harleen Deol to open for India. Lauren Bell to bowl first. A slip in place..
...THE CHASE...

India now faces a daunting task of chasing down 340 runs. This will test their batting skills and strategy. Despite the challenge, India will look to bounce back from this setback and prepare well for their upcoming ICC event around the horizon.We will be back with the chase in a while.

The hosts, India Women, will be concerned about their bowlers conceding over 300 runs. Kranti Gaud was the pick of the bowlers for picking up 3 wickets and she, along with Renuka Singh Thakur, were the standout performers for India. However, the team faces a bigger worry with Arundhati's injury, who was seen in a wheelchair after going off the field.

Amy Jones (39) and Heather Knight provided a solid foundation, while Nat Sciver-Brunt's century and Emma Lamb's knock of 84 helped the English side post a brilliant total. Sciver-Brunt retired out after her century, but Lamb's knock kept the hosts on the back foot. Once Lamb was dismissed, the Indian bowlers came back and took wickets in a flurry towards the end.

We have reached the halfway mark, with England Women posting an impressive total of 339. Despite losing Tammy Beaumont in the first over to Renuka's bowling, England's batting lineup performed well, thanks to a brilliant century from their skipper, Nat Sciver-Brunt and a handy knock from Emma Lamb.

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for an exciting match between India Women and England Women! Amy Jones and Tammy Beaumont are walking out to bat for England, while Renuka Thakur is ready to spearhead the Indian attack with the new ball.

Jemimah Rodrigues, the skipper of India Women, has won the toss and she chose to bowl first against England Women, captained by Nat Sciver-Brunt. Jemimah Rodrigues cited the challenge of seeing how the players will cope with these warm conditions and later how they'll pace the chase as the key factors in the decision to bowl first.

In other warm-up games, New Zealand Women are taking on India A Women in a warm-up match, showcasing the depth of the Indian squad. The White Ferns posted a total of 273/9 in their 50 overs. India A Women are currently chasing this target and are on track.

For England Women, captained by Nat Sciver-Brunt, these warm-up matches are pivotal in acclimatizing to the conditions. With the return of key players, Heather Knight from injury and Dani Wyatt from absence, they'll focus on finding their rhythm ahead of their next warm-up fixture against Australia. England's bowling unit, spearheaded by Lauren Bell, will face a tough challenge against India's potent batting lineup. Seeking to bounce back from their previous ODI series loss to India, England will look to these matches to gain momentum and build confidence. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

As the hosts, the Indian women's team is determined to make a strong statement in the World Cup. Following a mixed series against Australia, they've had an opportunity to introspect and fine-tune their game. With Smriti Mandhana in scintillating form, they'll aim to build on her momentum. However, they'll need to bolster their fielding and ensure their top-order batters capitalize on starts. With Jemimah Rodrigues set to return from illness and others seeking to find their footing, the India Women's team will be eager to showcase their true potential. Also, to see how Harmanpreet Kaur goes in the warm-up games before the showdown in the ICC event, she has not been at her best recently and her form will be key for the hosts.

Hello and welcome! We're excited for Match 4 of the ICC Women's World Cup warm-up fixtures, where the hosts, India Women, take on England Women. This match marks a crucial stage in the teams' preparations as they fine-tune their strategies ahead of the tournament.
... MATCHDAY ...

We are in the final stretch of preparations for the 2025 ICC Women’s World Cup, and the teams are looking to fine-tune their game plans. Match 4 of the official warm-up fixtures sees hosts India take on England at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 1 in Bengaluru. India’s build-up has been ideal in terms of quality of opposition, with no better challenge than facing Australia. While they lost the series, there were certainly positives for Harmanpreet Kaur’s side to take away. The pitches across the three games were flat as a pancake, so the bowlers can’t be judged too harshly, though there is still room for improvement in terms of control. Young Kranti Goud showed promise on those batting-friendly surfaces, while the likes of Renuka Singh Thakur, Arundhati Reddy, and Sneh Rana will be looking to use this contest against England, as well as the next one against New Zealand, to build rhythm and confidence. Renuka, in particular, will be keen to find her groove again after returning from an injury layoff. Perhaps more concerning than the bowling was the fielding. After showing marked improvement during the series in England earlier this year, old habits resurfaced, and India will be eager to tighten up in that department before the World Cup begins. In the batting department, Smriti Mandhana carried her excellent form, but the rest of the unit left plenty to be desired. Jemimah Rodrigues, who missed the last couple of games due to viral fever, will be aiming to return fit and firing. As for Pratika Rawal, Harmanpreet Kaur, Harleen Deol and Richa Ghosh, they all managed to get starts against Australia but failed to convert them into substantial scores. Against quality opposition like England and New Zealand in these warm-ups, they will be keen to turn those starts into meaningful contributions. Not that India do not need these warm-ups, but between the two sides in this clash, it is certainly England who stand to benefit more. Their last ODI outing came back in July, and while their players have been active in domestic cricket, they have been doing so in different teams rather than as a unit. Nat Sciver-Brunt’s side underwent a training camp in Abu Dhabi before arriving in India, and now face India first before taking on Australia in their two warm-up fixtures. England’s last ODI series in July saw them lose at home to India. Nat Sciver-Brunt shouldered most of the batting load in that series, while Sophia Dunkley and Emma Lamb chipped in, but without enough consistency. Their batting will get a major boost with the return of former skipper Heather Knight, whose experience against spin will be key to England’s campaign. Returning from a hamstring injury, these warm-up matches will be crucial for Heather, who has not played competitive cricket since May. Dani Wyatt also makes a return, while Alice Capsey features as well, with her off-breaks adding a handy bowling option. On the bowling front, the major talking point has been the non-selection of experienced seamer Kate Cross, leaving the pace attack relatively inexperienced. Lauren Bell, who enjoyed a successful Hundred campaign, will spearhead the attack, supported by Lauren Filer and Emily Arlott. It is a spin-heavy unit, with Sophie Ecclestone, Linsey Smith, Charlie Dean and Sarah Glenn in the ranks. Both Dean and Ecclestone also provide useful depth with the bat. The results matter little in these warm-up games, as it is more about ticking the boxes set out before the match and wrapping up the final stages of preparation.
